subject: Geography
description: Indian Scheduled Tribes — geographic distribution, constitutional provisions (Art 342, Fifth/Sixth Schedule), tribal arts, uprisings, PVTGs, PESA Act.

questions.stem: Which is the LARGEST Scheduled Tribe by population in India (Census 2011)?

options.option_text: Gond tribe of central India
Bhil tribe of western India
Santhal tribe of eastern India
Munda tribe of Chota Nagpur

questions.explanation: GOND TRIBE — largest Scheduled Tribe in India (~1.22 crore as per Census 2011). They inhabit the CENTRAL INDIAN HIGHLANDS — the historical 'Gondwana' region — spread across MADHYA PRADESH, MAHARASHTRA, CHHATTISGARH, TELANGANA, ANDHRA PRADESH, ODISHA. The supercontinent 'GONDWANA' is named after them (geological term coined by Eduard Suess, 1885). LANGUAGE: Gondi (Dravidian family). CULTURE: famous for Gond paintings (Jangarh Singh Shyam pioneered the modern style). RANKING — TOP TRIBES BY POPULATION: (1) Gond ~1.22 cr. (2) BHIL ~1.04 cr (Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat, Maharashtra). (3) SANTHAL ~70 lakh (Jharkhand, WB, Odisha). (4) MEENA ~50 lakh (Rajasthan, MP). (5) MUNDA ~22 lakh (Jharkhand). KEY STATS: total ST population ~10.45 crore (8.6% of India). Madhya Pradesh has the LARGEST ST population in absolute numbers; MIZORAM and NAGALAND are HIGHEST in PERCENTAGE (>90% tribal). LAKSHADWEEP has 95% ST population. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'largest tribe in India' is a 1-mark guarantee in SSC CGL, IBPS GA, RRB. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests tribal-population-distribution recall.

questions.stem: Under Article 342, who has the power to specify which tribes are 'Scheduled Tribes' for a state?

options.option_text: President of India via notification
Parliament with simple majority law
National Commission for STs (NCST)
State legislature on its own there

questions.explanation: ARTICLE 342 (Scheduled Tribes): the PRESIDENT OF INDIA, after CONSULTATION WITH THE GOVERNOR of the state, may by PUBLIC NOTIFICATION specify the tribes/communities deemed Scheduled Tribes for that state/UT. PARLIAMENT may then INCLUDE or EXCLUDE any tribe from this list by simple-majority law (ordinary legislation, not constitutional amendment). ARTICLE 341 mirrors this for Scheduled Castes. RESERVATION POLICY: STs get 7.5% reservation in central govt jobs, education, and proportionate share in legislatures. CRITERIA used by Lokur Committee (1965) for ST classification: (1) Indications of primitive traits. (2) Distinctive culture. (3) Geographic isolation. (4) Shyness of contact with outside community. (5) Backwardness. CONSTITUTIONAL SAFEGUARDS: Art 15(4), 16(4), 46, 244, 275, 330, 332, 335, 338A, 339, 342. NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR SCHEDULED TRIBES (NCST) — Art 338A, established 2004 (89th Amendment) by bifurcating the earlier joint SC-ST Commission. PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 341/342 distinction tested in UPSC, MPSC, CGL Tier-2.

questions.stem: The SANTHAL REBELLION ('HUL') of 1855 against British colonial rule was led by:

options.option_text: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu (brothers)
Birsa Munda with his followers
Tilka Manjhi and Paharia tribes
Tantya Bhil and Bhagoji Naik

questions.explanation: SANTHAL REBELLION (SANTHAL HUL) 1855 — one of India's earliest organized tribal uprisings against British colonial rule, zamindars, and exploitative moneylenders ('dikus'). LEADERS: SIDHU MURMU and KANHU MURMU — brothers from BHOGNADIH village (Sahibganj district, present-day Jharkhand). Two more brothers — Chand and Bhairav — also led contingents. Mobilized ~60,000 Santhals; declared independence on 30 JUNE 1855 (now observed as 'Hul Diwas' in Jharkhand). British retaliation: martial law; ~15,000-20,000 Santhals killed; Sidhu and Kanhu captured and hanged. OUTCOME — SANTAL PARGANAS TENANCY ACT, 1876: granted Santhal farmers protection from land alienation; the area still has a separate tenancy regime. 'HUL' = revolution in Santali language (Ol Chiki script). CONTRAST WITH OTHER TRIBAL REVOLTS: (1) BIRSA MUNDA's 'ULGULAN' (1899-1900) — Munda tribe in Chota Nagpur against missionaries+British; Birsa is 'Dharti Abba' (Father of Earth). (2) TILKA MANJHI (1780s) — earlier Paharia revolt. (3) TANTYA BHIL (late 19th c.) — Bhil chief, Robin-Hood figure of central India. (4) RAMPA REBELLION 1922 — Alluri Sitarama Raju, Andhra Koya tribes. PYQ ANGLE: tribal revolts perennial UPSC, SSC topic.

questions.stem: WARLI PAINTINGS — the famous monochrome tribal art form — originate from which state?

options.option_text: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik area)
Madhya Pradesh tribal belt also
Jharkhand (Santal Parganas zone)
Gujarat (Dang district region)

questions.explanation: WARLI PAINTING — visual art of the WARLI TRIBE living in the THANE, PALGHAR, NASHIK districts of MAHARASHTRA (and small communities in adjoining Gujarat & Dadra-Nagar-Haveli). STYLE: monochrome (white rice-paste motifs on RED-OCHRE mud walls) using simple geometric shapes — TRIANGLES (humans, mountains), CIRCLES (sun, moon), SQUARES (sacred enclosure), spirals. THEMES: harvest, hunting, wedding, fertility rites, daily life. RECOGNITION: granted GEOGRAPHICAL INDICATION (GI) tag in 2014; works displayed in major global museums. KEY ARTIST: JIVYA SOMA MASHE (Padma Shri 2011) — credited with bringing Warli art into the modern public sphere. OTHER MAJOR TRIBAL/FOLK ART FORMS (memorize for SSC/UPSC GA): (1) GOND PAINTING — MP (vibrant dots-and-lines, animals, mythology). (2) PITHORA — Bhil/Rathwa tribes, Gujarat (ritual marriage art). (3) SAURA — Odisha (Lanjia Saura tribe). (4) MADHUBANI — Bihar (Mithila region). (5) PATTACHITRA — Odisha/WB. (6) KALAMKARI — Andhra Pradesh. PYQ FREQUENCY: tribal-art-state mapping is a top SSC, UPSC, IBPS GA MCQ — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The SIXTH SCHEDULE of the Constitution provides for Autonomous District Councils in:

options.option_text: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha
Nagaland, Manipur, and Arunachal
All states with Fifth Schedule areas

questions.explanation: SIXTH SCHEDULE (Articles 244(2), 275(1)): provides for AUTONOMOUS DISTRICT COUNCILS (ADCs) and Regional Councils in tribal areas of FOUR NORTHEASTERN STATES — ASSAM, MEGHALAYA, TRIPURA, MIZORAM. ADCs have LEGISLATIVE (laws on land, forests, marriage, inheritance), JUDICIAL (intra-tribe disputes), and FINANCIAL powers within their territories. CURRENT ADCs: ASSAM — North Cachar Hills (Dima Hasao), Karbi Anglong, Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC). MEGHALAYA — Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills, Garo Hills ADCs. TRIPURA — Tripura Tribal Areas ADC. MIZORAM — Chakma, Mara, Lai ADCs. FIFTH SCHEDULE (Article 244(1)): covers Scheduled Areas in NINE OTHER STATES — Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha. KEY CONTRAST: Fifth Schedule = administered by Governor with TAC (Tribes Advisory Council); Sixth Schedule = elected ADCs with autonomous law-making. RECENT: Ladakh demand for Sixth Schedule status (Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike, March 2024) — government has not yet granted. PYQ FREQUENCY: Fifth vs Sixth Schedule distinction is top-5 polity MCQ in UPSC, MPSC, NEET-style civics.

questions.stem: Which of these tribes is classified as a PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUP (PVTG)?

options.option_text: Jarawa of the Andaman Islands
Gond of Madhya Pradesh region
Bhil of Rajasthan-MP-Gujarat belt
Santhal of the Santal Parganas

questions.explanation: PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUPS (PVTGs) — formerly called 'Primitive Tribal Groups' (PTGs); renamed in 2006 by Ministry of Tribal Affairs based on Xaxa Committee (2004) recommendations. CRITERIA: (1) Pre-agricultural level of technology (hunting-gathering). (2) Stagnant or declining population. (3) Very low literacy. (4) Subsistence-level economy. NUMBERS: 75 PVTGs identified across 18 states/UTs. NOTABLE PVTGs: (a) JARAWA — Andaman, ~250-400 members; live in 1,028 sq km reserve; the 'Andaman Trunk Road' controversy (cuts through their territory). (b) GREAT ANDAMANESE — ~50 survivors; severely endangered. (c) ONGE — Little Andaman, ~120. (d) SHOMPEN — Great Nicobar, ~200. (e) SENTINELESE — completely isolated; refused all contact; the John Allen Chau incident (Nov 2018, US missionary killed). (f) DONGRIA KONDH — Niyamgiri Hills, Odisha; landmark 2013 Supreme Court Vedanta case where Gram Sabhas vetoed bauxite mining. (g) CHENCHU — AP/Telangana, hunter-gatherers. (h) BIRHOR, ASUR — Jharkhand. (i) BAIGA — MP. SCHEMES: PVTG Development Mission, Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN, ₹24,104 cr launched Nov 2023). PYQ ANGLE: PVTG names + locations frequent in UPSC, SSC.

questions.stem: The PESA Act, 1996 is significant for tribal areas because it:

options.option_text: Extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas
Reserves seats for tribals in state cabinets
Grants tribals exemption from income tax
Sets up separate tribal courts in districts

questions.explanation: PESA = PANCHAYATS (EXTENSION TO SCHEDULED AREAS) ACT, 1996. CONTEXT: the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) extended Panchayati Raj to rural India — but EXCLUDED Fifth Schedule areas (tribal regions of 9 states). PESA filled this gap by EXTENDING Panchayati Raj provisions to FIFTH SCHEDULE AREAS, with safeguards for tribal traditions. KEY PROVISIONS: (1) GRAM SABHA = supreme decision-making body for tribal villages (NOT just Panchayat). (2) Gram Sabha consent REQUIRED for: land acquisition, mineral concessions, rehabilitation, minor forest produce management, minor water bodies. (3) Tribes Advisory Council oversees implementation. (4) No outsider can be granted exclusive rights over minor forest produce. (5) Power to prevent land alienation. (6) Reservation for STs in panchayats proportionate to population. STATES COVERED (9): Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha. CHALLENGE: weak implementation — many states have not yet notified PESA Rules. COMPLEMENTARY ACT: FOREST RIGHTS ACT, 2006 (FRA) — recognizes individual + community forest rights of tribes inhabiting forest land. PYQ FREQUENCY: PESA is a top-3 tribal-governance MCQ in UPSC, HJS, state PSC.

questions.stem: The Toda tribe, whose distinctive needlework 'Toda Embroidery' holds a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, primarily inhabits which hill region of India?

options.option_text: Kodagu Hills in Karnataka's Western Ghats region
Nilgiri Hills, straddling Tamil Nadu and Kerala
Palani Hills in the Dindigul district of Tamil Nadu
Anamalai Hills near Valparai in Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: The Toda are a pastoral tribe exclusive to the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu–Kerala border); their geometric embroidery received a GI tag. Palani Hills and Anamalai Hills are other Tamil Nadu ranges but are not Toda territory — a common geographic mix-up.

questions.stem: The Gondi language, spoken by the Gond — the largest tribal group by population — belongs to which language family, surprising given their central-Indian geography?

options.option_text: Indo-Aryan, like most languages of central India
Austro-Asiatic, same family as Santali and Mundari
Dravidian, related to languages like Telugu and Kannada
Tibeto-Burman, spoken mainly in northeast India

questions.explanation: Gondi belongs to the South-Central Dravidian branch, making it a linguistic island amid surrounding Indo-Aryan languages — a classic examiner trick. Santali and Mundari are Austro-Asiatic (the answer most candidates choose), but those are distinct tribal languages of Jharkhand.

questions.stem: The 'Dhokra' brass and bronze casting art, practiced by tribal artisans across Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh, employs which metal-working technique that dates back over 4,000 years?

options.option_text: Lost-wax (cire perdue) casting using a non-reusable clay mold
Sand casting, pouring molten metal into compacted sand molds
Die casting under high pressure in pre-formed steel molds
Sheet metal forming by alternating hammering and annealing

questions.explanation: Dhokra uses the lost-wax (cire perdue) process: a wax model is covered in clay, heated to melt the wax out, then molten metal is poured in — the mold is broken to release the piece, making every artifact unique. Sand casting and die casting are modern industrial methods, not the ancient Dhokra tradition.

questions.stem: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, legally recognising the rights of forest-dwelling communities over land and forest resources, was enacted in which year?

options.option_text: 2002, alongside the Wildlife Protection Amendment Act
2008, following a mid-term review of PESA Act outcomes
2006, after sustained advocacy by tribal rights movements
2013, alongside the Right to Fair Compensation Act

questions.explanation: The Forest Rights Act was passed in December 2006 (came into force 2008), correcting 'historical injustice' done to forest communities. 2002 is a common distractor as that year saw the Wildlife Protection Amendment; 2013 is associated with the Land Acquisition Act — both are plausible but wrong.

questions.stem: The 'Dhimsa' dance — performed in concentric circles during harvest festivals in the Eastern Ghats agency tracts — is primarily associated with which tribal community?

options.option_text: Gond communities of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh
Santhal community of Jharkhand's Chota Nagpur Plateau
Bodo tribes of Assam's Brahmaputra valley districts
Konda Dora and Jatapu tribes of the Visakhapatnam agency

questions.explanation: Dhimsa is the signature tribal dance of the Konda Dora, Jatapu, and related communities of Visakhapatnam and East Godavari agency areas in Andhra Pradesh. Its circular formation and rhythmic percussion are hallmarks. Santhal dances (Dong, Sohrai) and Gond dances are performed in central India — entirely different regions.

questions.stem: The Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) strategy — mandating that funds from Central and State Plans be allocated to tribal areas in proportion to their Scheduled Tribe population — was first operationalised during which Five Year Plan?

options.option_text: Third Five Year Plan (1961–66), introduced as Tribal Blocks
Fifth Five Year Plan (1974–79), as a dedicated tribal strategy
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969–74), after welfare commission reports
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980–85), following TSP performance review

questions.explanation: TSP was conceptualised and first implemented during the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974–79), inspired by the model of the Special Component Plan for SCs. The Fourth Plan (1969–74) is a tempting distractor because it saw the early tribal welfare frameworks, but TSP as a formal fund-flow mechanism began only in the Fifth Plan.

questions.stem: Denotified Tribes (DNTs), also called 'Vimukta Jatis', were historically branded hereditary criminals, surveilled, and required to register with the police under which British-era legislation that was repealed in 1952?

options.option_text: Suppression of Dacoity Act, 1905, targeting hereditary criminal gangs
Thuggee and Dacoity Suppression Acts enacted between 1836 and 1848
Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, branding entire communities as born criminals
Indian Forest Act, 1878, restricting tribal access to forest resources

questions.explanation: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 (extended and amended in 1911) declared specific nomadic and semi-nomadic communities 'criminal by birth', forcing them to register and restricting their movement. It was repealed in 1952 and replaced by Habitual Offenders Acts; the affected communities are now called DNTs/Vimukta Jatis. The Thuggee Acts are a plausible distractor but predate and differ in scope.
